suite_latency_expectation.notes: Eval cases measure whether an agent can drive the repo-like CLI, Workbench Cloud remotes, remote --remote execution, and eval authoring without relying on private remote implementation state.

evals.title: Verify or install Workbench
evals.prompt: Prepare Workbench access for this repo from scratch. Assume the `workbench` binary is not installed. Install the published package, verify the binary, authenticate to `https://v2.workbench.ai`, and report whether Workbench Cloud access is ready.
evals.expected_output: The response uses the Workbench skill, installs the published package only because the binary is missing, verifies the binary, starts the Workbench login flow, and explains that npm registry or auth failures should stop the cloud access flow cleanly.

assertions.text: reports install is conditional on a missing binary
reports registry or auth failures stop the cloud access flow cleanly

evals.title: Create a remote benchmark and apply a spec
evals.prompt: Create a remote Workbench benchmark named `invoice-parser`, push local source and runtime history idempotently, and report the benchmark id plus the push result.
evals.expected_output: The response targets a remote Workbench server, creates or selects a benchmark with the repo-like CLI, pushes local source plus runtime history, opens or returns the Workbench Cloud benchmark URL for an embedded browser, and reports remote benchmark metadata.

assertions.text: creates or updates a remote benchmark
reports that remote benchmark state is durable
opens or returns the Workbench Cloud benchmark URL

evals.title: Author an eval from an existing workflow
evals.prompt: Create a Workbench eval around an existing command `python scripts/check_report.py --tasks tasks --out result.json`. Write the source-shaped files, adapt the benchmark/candidate contract, validate `benchmark.yaml` and a candidate directory, and explain how to push and start one smoke run.
evals.expected_output: The response uses the Workbench skill eval-authoring docs, starts from the existing-workflow guide, writes version-4 `benchmark.yaml`, a candidate manifest such as `candidates/codex/candidate.yaml`, candidate files declared with `files: { path: files }` under `candidates/codex/files`, and optional candidate-owned `improve` settings with required benchmark `name`, `description`, and `engine`, uses `engine.use: workbench` with `engine.with.environment`, `engine.with.tasks.path` only when the native task directory is not `tasks/`, and `engine.with.score`, requires candidate `name`, `files`, and `runs`, and `candidate.improve.edits` plus an improve adapter when improve is needed, uses task `files/` for public fixtures staged at `paths.case` and task `tests/` for private verifier material staged at `paths.enginePrivate`, writes native task manifests with `version: 3` for the built-in Workbench engine, wraps the existing workflow with a candidate run adapter such as `codex`, uses the Workbench engine's `tests` scoring helper whose verifier writes `$WORKBENCH_TESTS_VERIFIER_DIR/reward.json` or `$WORKBENCH_TESTS_VERIFIER_DIR/reward.txt` with a finite reward, avoids hard-coded `/tests` or invented log roots, and uses `workbench check`, `workbench push`, and a smoke eval with an explicit candidate directory.

assertions.text: routes through the existing-workflow authoring guide
writes remote benchmark and candidate YAML

evals.title: Author an eval from file outputs
evals.prompt: Create a remote Workbench eval for a workflow that produces Office files from uploaded materials: a source DOCX, golden DOCX, and reference XLSX. Build tasks, choose an Office-capable runtime, keep the candidate as the mutable workflow, validate the spec, and describe the first smoke run.
evals.expected_output: The response uses the Workbench skill file-output task docs, chooses focused file recipes, keeps the candidate as the mutable workflow being improved, creates version-4 benchmark/candidate source plus version-3 task files with a candidate manifest declaring `files: { path: files }` and `runs`, uses `engine.use: workbench`, omits `engine.with.tasks` for the default `tasks/` directory or uses `engine.with.tasks.path` only for explicit native task selection, and writes native task manifests with `version: 3`, puts only supporting public file inputs under task `files/` for staging at `paths.case`, puts non-empty private verifier files under task `tests/` for staging at `paths.enginePrivate`, uses engine-owned rubric scoring for qualitative scoring by default, treats rubric scoring as one judge turn per criterion with `score.with.parallelism` as the throttle, uses engine-owned tests scoring only for deterministic checks or an existing scoring workflow, uses an Office-capable Dockerfile runtime through `engine.with.environment.dockerfile`, writes durable artifacts to `/workspace/output`, and validates the source before push/run commands.

assertions.text: routes through the file-output authoring guide
loads only the relevant file recipes
uses rubric scoring by default for qualitative file scoring

evals.title: Push source and start a remote run
evals.prompt: From an existing Workbench project with `candidates/codex` and `tasks`, push source and runtime history to a remote benchmark, start one remote improve run from base candidate id `candidate_123`, budget 1, and samples 1, watch it to terminal status, and report the run id and candidate id.
evals.expected_output: The response treats local directories as Workbench project source, pushes benchmark source plus runtime history, starts a remote improve run with `workbench improve --remote` and explicit `--base candidate_123`, watches the remote run, uses the returned URLs or `workbench open --remote` when browser navigation is needed, and reports the resulting run and candidate id.

assertions.text: pushes local source and runtime history
opens or returns the resulting candidate URL after the run when needed

evals.title: Inspect a local candidate snapshot
evals.prompt: List local candidate snapshots for a benchmark, list files for the selected candidate id, preview `SKILL.md`, and open the local Workbench UI without starting any remote mutation.
evals.expected_output: The response uses local `workbench candidates ...` inspection commands, opens or returns the read-only local Workbench URL with `workbench open --json --no-open`, and does not mutate remote state.

assertions.text: opens or returns the local Workbench URL

evals.title: Configure the remote API target
evals.prompt: Configure the CLI to target `https://v2.workbench.ai`, explain the environment-variable override for a one-off command, and state whether the user needs a git repository or preexisting local Workbench state.
evals.expected_output: The response uses workbench login or WORKBENCH_API_URL for remote API targeting and makes clear that git and preexisting local Workbench state are not required.

assertions.text: reports preexisting local Workbench state is not required
